messages:
alex: ran a bunch of nsys + perfetto captures for the kv-cache regression. kernel timeline looks noisy, NVTX ranges are all over the place so it's hard to map logical ops to kernels. anyone have a recommended NVTX naming convention?

ria: short version: include op, model, batch, and a short req-id. avoid very long strings (nsys/Perfetto truncates). also keep hot-path ranges coarse by default.

sam: agree with ria. example pattern we use in other projects: `op=model:batch:req` so something like `attn_fwd=redwood-13b:8:0x3f2a` — compact and parseable.

marta: important: decide which ranges are per-request vs per-batch. per-request KV cache checks are super noisy at scale. prefer a single `kv_check(batch=n)` range that contains per-request markers only when sampling or debug enabled.

alex: good call. i'm seeing thousands of `kv:lookup` NVTX pushes in the trace which I think is adding overhead and making timeline unreadable. how do we signal sampled fine-grained spans?

ria: put a sampling flag in runtime config, default 0.5-1%. when sampling is on, emit `nvtxRangePushA` for per-request spans and attach a concise id e.g. `req=3f2a`. also emit a top-level `request_span` that always exists.

sam: another tip: annotate kernel launches with logical kernel names if possible. for kernels invoked from our fused ops, set an NVTX range around the launch with names like `matmul_gemm:shard0` so the perf tool groups them. we used:```c
nvtxRangePushA("matmul_gemm:size=%d:bs=%d", M, B);
// kernel launch
nvtxRangePop();
```

marta: watch out for name length. Perfetto UI shows truncated labels in tracks; keeping under ~64 chars avoids clutter. also avoid characters that break CSV exports (commas, newlines).

alex: any conventions for delimiters and keys? i'm parsing traces downstream to auto-correlate nvtx->kernel.

ria: use `:` as main delimiter and `=` for key/values. stable key order: `op:model:bs:req` or `op:bs:model:req`. pick one and stick to it. e.g. `attn_red:13b:8:req=3f2a`. put req at end so sampled entries are easy to regex.

sam: for kernel selection work we also need to record the selected kernel variant id in the NVTX annotation (short numeric id). e.g. `attn:13b:8:kid=17` — that lets us map performance differences to selector decisions without parsing logs.

marta: plus include a coarse `seq` span at request start: `req=3f2a:seq=42` so we can join to application logs by seq. keep seq small (decimal).

alex: perf-bot uploaded the latest traces for 3 runs: 2026-03-12 nightly, 2026-03-13 post-change, 2026-03-14 stress.

perf-bot: Uploaded nsys traces to s3://redwood-perf/trace_1825001111_nightly.zip ; perfetto links: https://perfetto/trace/abc123 (private). :rocket:

ria: when you open the perfetto timeline, enable `nvtx` and `cuda` tracks, then filter by name regex `attn|matmul|kv`. that isolates the hot paths. also use `group by slice` to collapse repeated small ranges.

sam: small practical: don't put variable-length model names in the middle. make model short token like `r13` instead of `redwood-13b` if you need more info in UI. we had traces where long model names shifted layout.

alex: ok i'll push a tiny change to runtime: default sampling off, new NVTX name pattern `op:rmod:bs:kid:req` with rmod short model token, kid numeric. will add config to enable per-request NVTX for debug. i'll also add a note to the perf docs about truncation and sampling.

marta: :thumbsup: LMK when it's up, i'll re-run the stress captures and check kernel mapping.

trace-bot: FYI: cc @observability — we may want a baked-in mapping table for rmod->full model in the trace metadata export.

ria: last thing — we should avoid NVTX in tight inner loops that are launched millions of times. prefer to annotate the high-level op boundary instead of every micro-op. NVTX calls themselves can serialize and skew timings if overused.

alex: noted. thanks all — i'll open a small PR with the pattern, config, and an example trace link.
